edits.after_excerpt: For a diagram with $j$ basepoint pairs, regard its full filtered minus complex as a complex over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by restriction of scalars along $U\mapsto U_i$ for any one chosen basepoint variable. The resulting complexes of $\mathcal H_0$ and $\mathcal H_1$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb F_2[U]$, preserving relative Maslov grading and Alexander filtration, even when the diagrams have different numbers of basepoint pairs. The choice of the single variable action does not affect this type. Restriction retains the independent variables in the chain module; it is different from quotienting by $U_1=\cdots=U_j$. The latter ordinary quotient is the fully collapsed complex and has filtered chain homotopy type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(j-1)}$, where $V$ has zero differential and bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$. Equivalently, a basepoint stabilization before quotienting is modeled by the cone of $U_{j+1}+U_i$ on the polynomial extension of the old complex; after the simultaneous quotient this is a zero-map cone and contributes the displayed extra factor.

edits.before_excerpt: A free stabilization keeps the Heegaard surface fixed, adds one new $w$-point and one new $z$-point, and adds an $\alpha$-curve and a $\beta$-curve in a disk disjoint from the old curves and marked points; those new curves meet transversely in two points, with one new marked point in each of the two regions between them and the connecting arcs extended locally so the represented knot is unchanged.
edits.after_excerpt: A basepoint-pair (index-zero/three) stabilization keeps the genus fixed and adds one curve to each system and one $w,z$ pair along the represented knot. Its inverse removes the following elementary configuration, after relabeling the cyclic pairs: curves $\alpha_0,\beta_0$ bound disks $A_0,B_0$ on the surface, are disjoint from every opposite-system curve except each other, and intersect transversely in two points; $A_0\cap B_0$ is a bigon containing just $w_0$, while $A_0\setminus B_0$ contains just $z_0$ and $B_0\setminus A_0$ contains the next $z$-point along the cyclic pairing. Remove $\alpha_0,\beta_0,w_0,z_0$ and concatenate the adjacent trivial knot arcs. The surviving marked points stay fixed. Thus the move inserts a pair along an existing knot arc rather than adjoining an isolated marked component in an empty disk. Both descriptions include the simultaneous boundary-parallel arc systems and require the stated one-$w$, one-$z$ condition in each attaching complement.

edits.before_excerpt: Let $G$ and $G'$ be one-component grid diagrams related by one cyclic permutation, commutation, stabilization, or destabilization as defined in the grid-move theorem.
edits.after_excerpt: Let $G$ and $G'$ be one-component grid diagrams related by one of the following local moves. A cyclic permutation changes the planar cut of the toroidal grid by moving the first row or column to the last. A row commutation exchanges consecutive rows whose closed horizontal marking intervals are disjoint or strictly nested; a column commutation uses the same condition on vertical marking intervals. A stabilization replaces a marked cell by a two-by-two block with the original marking type in two opposite cells and the other type in a third cell, leaves the fourth cell empty, and inserts one row and one column, relocating the old companion markings so each new row and column has one mark of each type. Any of the four empty corners is allowed, and destabilization is the inverse move.
